newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dubinin says Russian currency policy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Dubinin says Russian currency policy unchanged.

text.p: Russian currency policy is unchanged and the rouble will probably continue to devalue roughly in line with inflation next year, Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Monday.
He was commenting on plans announced earlier to redenominate the rouble from the start of 1998 by stripping three zeroes off the currency, so that one new rouble will be worth 1,000 old ones.
"We have set our targets for currency policy for the beginning and end of the year and they remain in force," Dubinin told a news conference.

He said details of 1998 currency policy would be announced about a month before the end of this year, adding: "I don't see any reason for a dramatic change in currency policy for 1998. The gradual devaluation of the rouble will most likely continue in line with inflation."

Since mid-1995 the central bank has held the rouble in a pre-announced currency band, known as a corridor, allowing a gradual devalation. The mechanism is similar to a crawling peg devaluation, except that it is based on upper and lower limits rather than a central point.
For this year the bank has announced a set of daily upper and lower limits and within these it sets every day its own buying and selling rates for major banks.

The rouble has never moved outside the corridor limits and has only rarely strayed outside the central bank's own rates. The corridor will end the year at 5,750-6,350 per dollar after starting it at 5,500-6,100. The rouble is currently about 5,800 per dollar.
